{"candidate_rtl":"module mul_subexpression(
    input [7:0] multiplicand,
    input [7:0] multiplier,
    output [15:0] product
);
    wire [15:0] row0;
    wire [15:0] row1;
    wire [15:0] row2;
    wire [15:0] row3;
    wire [15:0] row4;
    wire [15:0] row5;
    wire [15:0] row6;
    wire [15:0] row7;

    assign row0 = {8'b0, multiplicand & {8{multiplier[0]}}};
    assign row1 = {8'b0, multiplicand & {8{multiplier[1]}}} << 1;
    assign row2 = {8'b0, multiplicand & {8{multiplier[2]}}} << 2;
    assign row3 = {8'b0, multiplicand & {8{multiplier[3]}}} << 3;
    assign row4 = {8'b0, multiplicand & {8{multiplier[4]}}} << 4;
    assign row5 = {8'b0, multiplicand & {8{multiplier[5]}}} << 5;
    assign row6 = {8'b0, multiplicand & {8{multiplier[6]}}} << 6;
    assign row7 = {8'b0, multiplicand & {8{multiplier[7]}}} << 7;

    wire [15:0] level1_0;
    wire [15:0] level1_1;
    wire [15:0] level1_2;
    wire [15:0] level1_3;
    wire [15:0] level2_0;
    wire [15:0] level2_1;
    wire [15:0] level3_0;

    assign level1_0 = row0 + row1;
    assign level1_1 = row2 + row3;
    assign level1_2 = row4 + row5;
    assign level1_3 = row6 + row7;
    assign level2_0 = level1_0 + level1_1;
    assign level2_1 = level1_2 + level1_3;
    assign level3_0 = level2_0 + level2_1;
    assign product = level3_0;
endmodule","bottleneck":"The prior single multiply expression can map through a long or tool-selected arithmetic network. The original and prior forms also expose a serial accumulation opportunity. The candidate makes the eight 16-bit partial-product operands explicit and reduces them through a balanced three-level adder tree, limiting carry-propagation depth from seven serial additions to three.","rewrite":"Preserve the unsigned partial-product construction and 16-bit arithmetic, but pair the eight shifted rows first, then pair those results, and perform one final addition. Constant shifts are wiring-only, while the balanced structure reduces the longest combinational path.","expected_timing_gain":"Expected improvement in maximum data arrival, especially for multiplier-bit inputs, because the partial-product AND delay is followed by at most three dependent 16-bit additions instead of seven. The exact gain depends on ABC rewriting and SKY130 cell selection.","area_or_other_cost":"The design uses the same seven 16-bit additions as the serial accumulation and the same 64 partial-product AND functions, so mapped area should remain close to the prior implementation and below the stated cap. It adds only interconnect and intermediate nets.","functional_boundaries":"All inputs are treated as arbitrary unsigned 8-bit binary values. Every intermediate and the output are 16 bits, matching the original truncation behavior. The balanced reassociation is equivalent because 16-bit addition is associative modulo 2^16, and the true unsigned product already fits in 16 bits."}
